title: Variable set but never read
description:
Unused-code rule — a variable is written but never read anywhere in the catalog. Dead weight at best; at worst the reading side was renamed and the write now goes nowhere. Known false-positive classes: values handed on as script parameters, variable names assembled at runtime, and reads that happen outside the exported files — the rule is therefore informational, not an error.

Based on the fmCheckMate check "ListVarsDefinedButUnused" — https://github.com/mrwatson-de/fmCheckMate-XSLT
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: A variable nobody reads costs nothing at runtime but misleads every reader of the script: it looks like state that matters. It is also the visible half of a renaming that was only carried through on one side.
rule.remediation: Remove the assignment, or restore the read side if the value is still meant to be used. Check first whether the value leaves the script as a parameter or is read under a name built at runtime.

meta.calibration: Built on the import-time variable resolution instead of the source's substring search over calculation text, which makes the read side far more reliable. Counts are aggregated over the variable's own scope key — script for local variables, file for globals.
